user-code-on-own-domain-01.graded_text: The target layout serves people's HTML and JavaScript from a separate registrable domain, not from any subdomain of plinth.example.

votes.e: A/project/docs/hosting-plan.md target table keeps user code on the product's registrable domain: "| User apps | `<name>.plinth.example` | Unchanged for users. One origin per app. No Plinth credentials on this domain. |" and "The signed-in product and its auth move instead." People's HTML/JS is still served from subdomains of plinth.example; the product moves to `<product-domain>`, not the user code.

user-code-on-own-domain-02.graded_text: The reason given is that every subdomain of one registrable domain is the same site: script on a sibling subdomain can set cookies for the parent domain and ride same-site requests, which lets it interfere with sign-in (login CSRF or session confusion) or reach session tokens.

votes.e: A/project/docs/hosting-plan.md: "Every `<name>.plinth.example` is *same-site* with `app.plinth.example`. `SameSite` cookies are still sent on requests from an app to the product"; "Any app can set `Domain=plinth.example` cookies. These can shadow or fix the product's own cookies and break or hijack sign-in"; "any app's script can read `document.cookie` and send the token somewhere else".

user-code-on-own-domain-03.graded_text: The short <name>.plinth.example address is kept as Plinth's own page, which frames the app served from the other domain, so visitors still see the Plinth address.

votes.e: A/project/docs/hosting-plan.md never makes the short address a Plinth-owned page framing content from another domain; user HTML stays top-level: "| User apps | `<name>.plinth.example` | Unchanged for users." Framing appears only in non-chosen option C: "A Plinth shell is the top-level page. The user's HTML runs in a frame" on the same hosts.

user-code-on-own-domain-04.graded_text: Each app gets its own origin on the content domain, such as a label per app, so one app cannot read another's storage.

votes.e: A/project/docs/hosting-plan.md: "each app has **its own origin**. That keeps `localStorage`, IndexedDB, and service workers isolated between apps without extra work. Never move apps onto paths under one shared host." plus table row "One origin per app" on the user-app domain, which in A's target holds "No Plinth credentials" (the content-only domain).

user-code-on-own-domain-05.graded_text: Until the separate domain can be set up after the freeze, people's code runs with an opaque origin, through a sandbox (for example a CSP sandbox header) without allow-same-origin, and the plan says this costs the apps their browser storage. It does not keep serving people's code as the top-level document on plinth.example subdomains during the beta.

votes.e: A/project/docs/hosting-plan.md lists the opaque-origin sandbox only as an alternative under "## Owner decision needed": "C. Sandbox user code on its current hosts ... `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox allow-scripts allow-forms allow-popups allow-modals` (no `allow-same-origin`)" while recommending "**A. One freeze exception (recommended)**". A/answer.txt: "**C:** run app code in a locked-down frame." Not chosen; absent an owner decision the beta keeps user code as the top-level document on plinth.example subdomains.
